images.title: Four right angles
images.purpose: Show two tilted lines that cross so that all four angles are 90 degrees, so tilt does not matter.
images.composition: Two long tilted lines crossing at the centre of a white frame, with a small square mark in each of the four corners.
exact_structure: Line l (teal #0072B2) tilted about 30 degrees above the horizontal, rising to the right.
Line m (amber #E69F00) crossing l at the centre point at exactly 90 degrees, so it falls to the right at about 60 degrees below the horizontal.
Four small squares, one in each of the four angles at the crossing, each filled light reddish purple (#CC79A7).
Each of the four angles is labelled 90 degrees, close to the corner.
Neither line is horizontal or vertical.
Line names l and m sit at the far ends.
rejection: any angle not drawn as a right angle
fewer or more than 4 square marks
images.takeaway: Four equal angles at a crossing are each 90 degrees, and the lines are perpendicular however they are tilted.
images.description: Two tilted lines crossing with a square mark and the number 90 degrees in each of the four angles.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Students check that all four angles are the same, and each is a right angle.

image_decisions.why: The tilted pair shows that perpendicular does not mean upright.
